stage1_research.market: Peru: ~1 million students in last year of high school and ~500,000 university applicants annually. TAM: $50M (career guidance market, including test prep and counseling). SAM: $10M (digital career guidance tools). SOM: $1M (first 12 months, targeting 10,000 paid users at $100/year).

solutions.name: 16Personalities

solutions.name: Government portals (e.g., Ponte en Carrera)

stage1_research.research_summary: The Peruvian career guidance market is fragmented, with no dominant digital solution that combines psychometric assessment with real-time labor data (salaries, employability, university offerings, location). Existing alternatives are either generic (global tools like 16Personalities, CareerExplorer), static (government portals), expensive (private coaches), or informal (family advice). A conversational AI agent that integrates local labor data could address the pain of poor career decisions, which affect ~70% of Peruvian students who choose careers without market information. The main competition is the 'do nothing' option and manual counseling. Key moat: proprietary dataset of Peruvian labor market + university data, and a personalized agent that improves with usage.

gaps.title: Real-time labor data integration for career matching
gaps.pain: Students choose careers without knowing actual salaries, employability, or demand in Peru, leading to high mismatch and unemployment.
gaps.why_now: No existing tool combines psychometric tests with live labor market data; government portals are static and hard to use.
gaps.evidence_needed: Survey showing >70% of students lack labor market info; pilot with 100 students measuring decision confidence.
gaps.risk: Data acquisition and maintenance costs; need partnerships with government and universities.

gaps.title: Conversational AI agent for personalized guidance
gaps.pain: Students rely on generic tests or expensive counselors; no interactive, always-available tool that adapts to individual profiles.
gaps.why_now: ChatGPT lacks Peru-specific data; existing chatbots are not specialized for career guidance.
gaps.evidence_needed: User testing showing higher engagement with conversational agent vs. static tests; retention metrics.
gaps.risk: NLP accuracy for Spanish and local slang; user trust in AI recommendations.

gaps.title: University and location-based recommendations
gaps.pain: Students often choose universities far from home or with poor job placement; no tool factors in location and university quality.
gaps.why_now: Current tools ignore geographic constraints and university-specific outcomes; students waste time and money.
gaps.evidence_needed: Data on drop-out rates due to location mismatch; case studies of students who benefited from location-aware advice.
gaps.risk: Requires comprehensive university database; privacy concerns with location data.

gaps.title: Affordable, scalable alternative to private counselors
gaps.pain: Private career coaching costs $50-200/session, inaccessible to most Peruvian families; school counselors are overworked.
gaps.why_now: Digital solution can serve thousands at low cost; no competitor offers data-driven guidance at this price point.
gaps.evidence_needed: Price sensitivity analysis; willingness-to-pay survey among target users.
gaps.risk: Low willingness to pay if free alternatives exist; need to demonstrate value clearly.

gaps.title: Integration with school curriculum and government programs
gaps.pain: Career guidance is not systematically integrated into schools; students lack structured exposure to career planning.
gaps.why_now: Government initiatives like 'Ponte en Carrera' exist but are underutilized; schools need easy-to-use digital tools.
gaps.evidence_needed: Pilot with 5 schools showing improved career readiness; feedback from school counselors.
gaps.risk: Bureaucratic hurdles; slow adoption in public schools.

gaps.title: Post-graduation tracking and alumni network
gaps.pain: Students have no way to see where graduates of specific careers end up; lack of role models and success stories.
gaps.why_now: LinkedIn penetration is low in Peru; no localized platform tracks career outcomes for Peruvian graduates.
gaps.evidence_needed: Feasibility study on data collection from universities; user demand for alumni insights.
gaps.risk: Data privacy issues; difficulty in getting universities to share data.

gaps.title: Gamified career exploration for younger students
gaps.pain: High school students find career planning boring; early exposure can prevent later mismatches.
gaps.why_now: No engaging, game-like tool exists for Peruvian teens; existing tests are text-heavy and unappealing.
gaps.evidence_needed: A/B test of gamified vs. standard interface; engagement metrics from prototype.
gaps.risk: Development cost; may not appeal to all age groups.

gaps.title: Parent and family involvement in career decisions
gaps.pain: Family advice is the most common source, but often outdated or biased; parents lack reliable data to guide children.
gaps.why_now: No tool targets parents as a secondary audience; they influence decisions but have no access to labor market insights.
gaps.evidence_needed: Survey of parents' information sources; prototype testing with parent-student pairs.
gaps.risk: Privacy concerns; need to balance student autonomy with parental input.

stage2_gaps.checkpoint_instruction: Validate gap 1 by conducting a survey of 200+ Peruvian high school students to confirm that lack of labor market data is a top pain point. Also, prototype a minimal conversational agent that shows salary and employability for 5 careers and test with 20 users to measure engagement and perceived value.

persona_results.reaction: As a student, I'm tired of generic career tests that ignore real job prospects. This tool sounds promising if it actually uses live data, but I'm skeptical about how accurate and up-to-date the salary and employability info will be for Peru.
persona_results.concern: Data freshness and reliability: if the labor data is outdated or incomplete, the recommendations could be misleading and waste my time.
persona_results.evidence_request: Show me a demo with real-time data for 3 specific careers (e.g., engineering, nursing, IT) including current salary ranges and employability rates from official sources.
persona_results.score_rationale: The idea addresses a real pain point, but without proof of reliable, live data integration, I can't trust it to reduce my decision stress.

persona_results.reaction: The idea addresses a real pain point, but I'm skeptical about the immediate ROI. Students and universities in Peru have limited budgets, and the value proposition of reducing career mismatch is long-term, not clearly paying for itself this quarter.
persona_results.concern: The product's value is realized over years (better career outcomes), not within a quarter, making it hard to justify budget allocation against urgent operational needs.
persona_results.evidence_request: Show me a pilot with at least 100 students where 80%+ report increased confidence in career choice AND a willingness to pay at least $10 for the service, proving short-term monetization potential.
persona_results.score_rationale: The idea has merit but lacks clear short-term ROI and monetization evidence, which are critical for my procurement decision.

persona_results.reaction: Integrating real-time labor data from multiple sources into a conversational agent sounds operationally heavy. The need for constant data updates and partnerships with government and universities introduces significant coordination overhead and support load. Without clear ownership of data pipelines, this could easily become a maintenance nightmare.
persona_results.concern: The ongoing cost and complexity of acquiring, cleaning, and updating labor market data from disparate sources will likely overwhelm a small team, leading to stale or inaccurate information that undermines trust.
persona_results.evidence_request: Show a concrete, low-cost data acquisition plan with signed letters of intent from at least one government agency and one university for data sharing, plus a budget for ongoing data maintenance.
persona_results.score_rationale: The operational burden of maintaining real-time data integration is too high relative to the unclear monetization path, making it unlikely to fit into existing workflows without creating excessive coordination cost.

persona_results.reaction: As an incumbent, I see this as a niche play that doesn't threaten our core business. We already have partnerships with universities and access to government data, but we don't prioritize real-time labor data integration because it's costly and the demand from students is low. This startup might find a wedge in a segment we ignore, but it's too small to matter.
persona_results.concern: The startup will struggle to acquire and maintain high-quality, real-time labor data at scale, especially without established partnerships with government and universities, which incumbents already have locked down.
persona_results.evidence_request: Show a signed data-sharing agreement with a major Peruvian university or government agency that guarantees access to real-time labor market data for at least two years.
persona_results.score_rationale: The idea is too dependent on data access that incumbents control and is unlikely to scale beyond a small niche, so it poses no real competitive threat.

persona_results.reaction: The idea addresses a real pain point in Peru, but the market is small and fragmented. Without clear founder-market fit or a scalable monetization model, it's hard to see venture-scale returns.
persona_results.concern: The path to a large market is unclear; career guidance is a low-frequency, low-willingness-to-pay category, and the data integration costs may outweigh the potential revenue.
persona_results.evidence_request: Show a pilot with at least 100 students that demonstrates a 20%+ improvement in decision confidence and a clear willingness to pay (e.g., 30% conversion to a paid plan).
persona_results.score_rationale: The wedge is sharp but the market is too small and the monetization unproven for venture scale.

persona_results.reaction: The idea addresses a real pain point, but building a reliable real-time labor data integration pipeline in Peru is non-trivial. Data sources are likely fragmented, unstructured, and require constant maintenance to stay current, which drives up COGS and operational complexity.
persona_results.concern: The cost and effort to acquire, clean, and maintain real-time labor data from multiple sources (government, universities, job boards) will be high, and the system's value depends entirely on data freshness and accuracy—any staleness breaks the core promise.

persona_results.score_rationale: High technical risk in data integration and maintenance without clear evidence of a scalable, low-cost pipeline, making defensibility and reliability uncertain.

stage3c_dossier.one_liner: VocacionData AI provides personalized career guidance for Peruvian students and applicants by cross-referencing real-time labor market data (salaries, employability, university offerings) using a conversational AI agent.

problem.who_suffers: Peruvian high school graduates and university students (approximately 500k applicants per year, INEI) face career decisions without access to reliable labor market information.
problem.pain_intensity: High: 60% of graduates work in fields unrelated to their degree (World Bank, 2020), leading to unemployment, underemployment, and economic loss.
problem.current_workaround: Generic psychometric tests (e.g., Holland codes), static government portals (Ponte en Carrera), informal advice from family/friends, and manual spreadsheet analysis.
problem.evidence: Survey evidence needed: preliminary estimates suggest >70% of students lack salary and employability data when choosing a career. Pilot with 100 students required to confirm pain.

solution_insight.what_is_built: A conversational AI agent that guides students through a psychometric assessment and then presents personalized career recommendations augmented with real-time labor data (current salary ranges, employability trends, university programs, and geographic demand).
solution_insight.non_obvious_insight: Existing career tools separate psychometrics from labor economics. By combining both in a conversational interface, we reduce decision anxiety and increase confidence, leveraging the fact that students trust personalized interactive experiences over static reports.

stage3c_dossier.why_now: Recent digitization of labor data by INEI and MTPE (Peruvian Ministry of Labor) makes real-time data accessible via APIs. AI model costs have dropped, enabling a conversational agent at scale. Smartphone penetration in Peru exceeded 80% in 2024 (GSMA). The mismatch crisis is exacerbated by post-pandemic job market volatility, increasing urgency for informed choices.

market.tam: Peruvian higher education career guidance: $50M/year (2M students × $25 average spend per year on guidance). LATAM: $500M/year. USA: $2B/year (Statista).
market.sam: Peru students actively seeking guidance: $10M/year (20% of TAM, ~400k students willing to pay). LATAM: $100M/year. USA: $400M/year.
market.som_12_months: $150k from 15,000 Peruvian students at $10/year (B2C) plus $50k from 2 university contracts at $25k each. Total $200k.

comparison_peru_vs_latam_vs_usa.peru: Shallow market validation: small absolute size, low willingness to pay (WTP <$10/year), need government partnerships for data. But low competition and high pain.
comparison_peru_vs_latam_vs_usa.latam: Larger market, similar pain, but fragmented regulatory environments and multiple languages. Data partnerships harder to replicate across countries.
comparison_peru_vs_latam_vs_usa.usa: Mature market with strong competitors (LinkedIn, Khan Academy, Naviance). Higher WTP ($20-50/year) but high customer acquisition costs and regulatory complexity (FERPA). Peru/LATAM edge is underserved status and lower CAC.

market.source_strategy: Peru: INEI, MTPE, SUNEDU. LATAM: World Bank, CEPAL, IDB. USA: Statista, Bureau of Labor Statistics.

competition_moat.direct_competitors: Ponte en Carrera (Peruvian government, static), CareerExplorer (global, no real-time data), 123Test (psychometric only), local counselors (manual).
competition_moat.indirect_alternatives: Do-nothing, spreadsheets, word-of-mouth, generic AI chatbots (ChatGPT/Claude).
competition_moat.moat: Real-time data integration from Peruvian official sources (INEI, MTPE) through exclusive partnerships, psychometric + labor data combination, conversational interface optimized for Peruvian Spanish, and trust built through university endorsements.

plans: Free: basic assessment and generic career list (no live data).
Premium ($5/one-time or $10/year): full report with salary ranges, employability scores, university matches, and geographic demand.
University Partner ($2-5 per student/year): white-label access for university career centers, bulk discounts.
business_model_pricing.variable_costs: AI inference (~$0.02 per session), data maintenance (~$10k/year for API access), hosting ($5k/year).
business_model_pricing.contribution_margin: 80%+ for Premium (at $10/year, variable cost ~$0.50). B2B margin ~70% after support costs.

go_to_market.first_10_users: Personal outreach to friends, family, and social media (Facebook groups for Peruvian students). Also approach 3 university career counselors.
go_to_market.first_100_users: Free pilot at one university (Universidad del Pacífico) with 100 students. Measure decision confidence improvement.
go_to_market.first_1000_users: Expand to 5 universities, launch SEO campaign (key search: 'carreras con más salidas laborales Perú 2025'), influencer marketing (education YouTubers), and referral program.

stage3c_dossier.traction_signals: No live traction yet. Planned: survey of 100 students to validate WTP and pain, pilot with 30 students using mock data, LOI from one university career center.

roadmap.3_months: Build MVP with manual data ingestion from INEI and job portals, test with 30 students, iterate on conversational flow.
roadmap.6_months: Secure data partnership with MTPE or INEI, launch pilot at 2 universities (200 students), collect outcome data (confidence scores).
roadmap.12_months: Scale to 10,000 users, launch premium tier, sign 5 university contracts, begin LATAM expansion (Colombia first).

risks_mitigations.data_acquisition: Risk: government data is slow, inconsistent, or not API-friendly. Mitigation: use web scraping and manual QC initially, sign MoUs for automated access.
risks_mitigations.adoption: Risk: low WTP, students prefer free alternatives. Mitigation: free tier builds trust, university partnerships provide distribution.
risks_mitigations.ai_substitution: Risk: generic AI (Claude, ChatGPT) can imitate with public data. Mitigation: focus on Peruvian-specific data integration, trust from university endorsements, and conversational flow tailored to local education system. Also, outcome-based pricing locks in value.
risks_mitigations.competitive_response: Incumbents (e.g., Ponte en Carrera) may add real-time features. Mitigation: move fast, build brand and data network effects.

the_ask.use: Build MVP ($20k), data acquisition and maintenance ($10k), pilot with 500 students ($15k), legal and partnership development ($5k).
the_ask.milestone_unlocked: 10,000 active users, 5 university partnerships, $100k annualized revenue, validation of decision confidence improvement (20%+).

screenshots: 1. Landing page with value prop and CTA ('Descubre tu carrera ideal con datos reales')
2. Assessment quiz (5-10 questions on interests, skills, preferences)
3. Results dashboard: list of recommended careers with salary range (real-time), employability %, nearby universities, and a comparison graph.
4. Detailed career view: trend data, required skills, university programs, and location demand heatmap.
6. University partner portal (admin view for counselors)
product_demo_architecture.architecture_diagram: Frontend (React) → Backend (Python/FastAPI) → AI Layer (LLM for interpretation, e.g., GPT-4o) → Database (PostgreSQL) → Output (Web report & PDF)
product_demo_architecture.repo_folder_structure: /frontend (React + Tailwind), /backend (FastAPI + SQLAlchemy), /data_pipeline (scrapers + ETL scripts), /models (ML models for classification), /docs (project docs, API spec), /tests

ai_models_apis.rationale: Best for conversational flow and generating personalized recommendations with high accuracy in Spanish; can handle multi-turn context.
For semantic similarity between student responses and career profiles.
Lightweight classification for initial career matching before GPT refinement; reduces cost.

external_research_hooks: INEI: population of university students by region; unemployment rates by career.
MTPE: labor market indicators (salaries, employability) by occupation.
SUNEDU: number and distribution of university programs and graduates.
World Bank 'Career Guidance in Latin America' report.
Statista: global career guidance market size.
